newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Truck bomb destroys Colombian police station.
newsitem.headline: Truck bomb destroys Colombian police station.

text.p: A powerful truck bomb destroyed most of a police station in Colombia's oil production centre of Barrancabermeja on Thursday in the latest high-profile attack that authorities blamed on leftist rebels.
The blast was the second to tear through a police headquarters since Tuesday, when nine policemen were killed and 10 others were injured in an explosion outside a police headquarters in Bogota.

Col. Eduardo Martinez of the Barrancabermeja police said a dump truck was abandoned seconds before the pre-dawn explosion about 16 feet (five metres) from the front of the police station by a man who ran off under cover of darkness down a rain-swept street.

The explosion from the truck -- which was laden with sand -- destroyed about 70 percent of the police station and seriously damaged other buildings nearby, Martinez said, adding that none of the more than 20 police officers inside the building was seriously injured.
Local radio reports said at least five civilians were injured, however, by the bomb that was comprised of at least 110 pounds (50 kg) of dynamite.

Gen. Alfredo Salgado Mendez, a senior National Police official, said the bombing had all the hallmarks of an attack by one of the country's two leading guerrilla groups and added that authorities suspected that it was linked to Tuesday's blast in Bogota.
At least six rebels have been arrested in connection with the attack in the capital, including a man detained on Wednesday night on the Magdalena river just outside Barrancabermeja.

The city, which is the capital of northern Santander province and Colombia's main oil production centre, has a long history as a hotbed of rebel activity and the National Liberation Army (ELN) is especially active in the area.

Founded by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966, the ELN specialises in kidnappings and attacks on oil and coal facilities. Colombia's main oil pipeline has been closed shut down since Sunday because of back-to-back ELN bombings.
In other developments, police said they killed six highway robbers in a pre-dawn shootout on Thursday outside Valledupar, capital of northern Cesar province.

The robbers had set up a roadblock about seven miles (12 km) outside of the city and had already held up the drivers of two cars when they made the mistake of stopping a carload of judicial police who gunned them down.
